newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's ASC looks into Fairfax trading.
newsitem.headline: Australia's ASC looks into Fairfax trading.

text.p: The Australian Securities Commission (ASC) said on Friday it applied to the Corporations and Securities Panel for a declaration that certain trading in John Fairfax Holdings Ltd shares by Merrill Lynch and Brierley Investments Ltd was unacceptable conduct.

Brierley acquired 19.9 percent of Fairfax on December 16, 1996. In February, Fairfax shareholders rejected a proposal that the New Zealand investment group be permitted to purchase a further 4.9 percent of the newspaper publisher, the ASC said.
As a consequence Brierley was unable to rely on the three percent creep rule in the Corporations Law to acquire further Fairfax shares until six months after December 31, 1996.

"An investigation by the ASC has revealed that Merrill Lynch (Australia) Futures Ltd and a subsidiary of BIL (Brierley) entered swap arrangements in respect of approximately 4.9 percent of Fairfax shares in March 1997," the ASC said.
ASC said a parcel of about 4.9 percent of Fairfax shares had been acquired by an entity in the Merrill Lynch group in January 1997.
Merrill Lynch sold about 22.5 million Fairfax shares or about three percent of the media group's issued capital on June over three days, June 17, 24 and 27, the ASC said.
Between June 17 and July 4 a subsidiary or susidiaries of Brierley purchased about the same number of Fairfax share through the Australian Stock Exchange, it said.
Fairfax shares closed three cents up at A$3.19.
